solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Phlegmatic type almost shut in thus

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in the middle of the word meaning thus

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed
a door pushed to is closed or nearly so, hence to

explanation.surface: Someone unexcitable has been all but locked inside, and takes it calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: TO, as in a door pulled to, goes 'in' SIC. 'Phlegmatic type' is the definition; it is a noun phrase, so the answer is a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures hardship without showing emotion, which is exactly what a phlegmatic person is like.

clue.text: Hospital doctor originally operating in Sumatra

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered
points to the first letter of operating only

explanation.surface: A medic who first practised in Sumatra ran a clinic there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun in the medical scene but is a verb: rearrange O (from 'originally operating') with IN SUMATRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanatorium is a medical establishment for long-term patients, a kind of hospital.

clue.text: Choose to put up around centre of Newport

indicators.note: the upturned word goes round the middle letter
in a down clue, putting up a word reads it from the bottom upwards
picks the central letter of Newport

explanation.surface: Deciding to settle on the middle of a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns TO into OT, which goes 'around' P, the centre of NEWPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to make a choice between alternatives, so it means choose.

clue.text: Reddish church at top of hill

indicators.note: in a down clue the church sits above the hill word

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rise is a hill or slope

explanation.surface: A church with a rosy glow stands on the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a bright cherry-red colour, so it describes something reddish.

clue.text: Live at end of lake with beadle — a worker, possibly

parts.note: Mr Bumble is the parish beadle in Dickens's Oliver Twist
to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: signals taking only the final letter of the word lake

explanation.surface: A beadle lives out his days by a lake, as a working man might.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumble is the beadle in Oliver Twist. 'possibly' marks the definition as an example: a worker bee may be a bumblebee.
explanation.definitionFit: Among bumblebees, as with honeybees, many members of a colony are sterile female workers.

clue.text: Considerable criticism gathering round extreme parts of Henry's life

indicators.note: the word for considerable gathers the round letter into itself

parts.note: big means considerable
O is round in shape
rap is slang for blame or criticism, as in take the rap

indicators.note: the outermost letters of Henry, first and last

explanation.surface: Henry's story draws plenty of flak from all sides.
explanation.walkthrough: BIG 'gathering' O gives BIOG; then RAP and HY, the 'extreme parts of Henry'. The 's links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A biography is a written account of someone's life, so a life in the literary sense.

clue.text: Cheeseparer, one initially swimming in sea off Nice

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the French sea word

parts.note: mer is French for sea, and Nice is in France
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of swimming

explanation.surface: A tightwad has a first dip in the Mediterranean off the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off Nice' tells you to use French: MER. A cheeseparer is a stingy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeseparer is someone mean with money, which is just what a miser is.

clue.text: Tough left restaurant, having consumed hot starter

indicators.note: the eatery takes the letter inside, as if eating it

parts.note: an eatery is an informal word for a restaurant

indicators.note: the first letter of hot, as a starter begins a meal

explanation.surface: The steak was chewy, so we walked out of the restaurant after a spicy first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery meat or skin is hard and chewy, so leathery is a synonym of tough.

clue.text: Good French painter capturing old man, an emperor's supporter

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: the painter word holds the father word inside it

parts.note: a painter is an artist
one's old man is one's father, pa

explanation.surface: A fine French artist paints his father and is a loyal follower of an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: BON then ARTIST 'capturing' PA. The emperor is Napoleon Bonaparte.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bonapartist supported Napoleon Bonaparte, Emperor of the French, or his dynasty's claim.

clue.text: Not entirely secure as top bridge-player

indicators.note: the answer is only part of the run of words secure as top

explanation.surface: Not wholly confident as the leading card player.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'secure as top'. In bridge the four players are named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: In contract bridge the seats are North, South, East and West, so East is a bridge player.

clue.text: Infamous old port protected by other people?

indicators.note: the inner piece is shielded inside the phrase for other people

parts.note: other people are, whimsically, not us
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, often just Rio

explanation.surface: A disreputable old harbour town is kept safe by outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'other people' as a description of those who are not us is playful rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious and infamous are synonyms: both mean widely known for something bad.

clue.text: Woman's contribution finally accepted by Times

indicators.note: the letter is taken in by the word for times, sitting inside it

parts.note: ages are long periods, or times

indicators.note: signals only the closing letter of contribution

explanation.surface: A woman's piece for the newspaper is at last taken by The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is AGES; the definition is just 'Woman', with 's linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman in crossword convention.

clue.text: Surprisingly their purser's accepting a fund manager's position

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take in the single letter, enclosing it
an unexpected arrangement of the words their purser's is signalled

explanation.surface: Unexpectedly, the ship's purser has taken on a job looking after the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges THEIR PURSERS, and that rearrangement 'accepting' takes A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer looks after an organisation's funds, so the office of treasurer is a fund manager's post.

clue.text: Church body upset over spirit audibly fading away

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset word is turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

indicators.note: the word for spirit is to be heard, then spelt another way

parts.note: an essence is the spirit or distilled core of something

explanation.surface: A congregation is disturbed as a ghost slowly vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: NAVE 'upset' gives EVAN; ESSENCE said 'audibly' gives ESCENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Evanescence is the quality of quickly vanishing; the noun matches 'fading away' used as a noun.

clue.text: Remove monastic devotee adopting revised rite

indicators.note: the devotee word takes in the shuffled letters

parts.note: an oblate is a lay person dedicated to a monastic life

indicators.note: the word rite is altered, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Get rid of a monk who has taken up a reformed ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges RITE to ITER, which OBLATE is 'adopting'.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to destroy or erase completely, so it is a strong synonym of remove.

clue.text: Genuine old Spanish coin

definitions.meaning: a silver coin of Spain for centuries

explanation.surface: A historic coin from Spain turns out not to be a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Real is both an adjective for authentic and the name of a former Spanish currency unit.

clue.text: Marine creature reportedly saw a taxi crossing river

indicators.note: signals that the words saw a are rendered by how their synonym is said

parts.note: saw a means spied a, which in a non-rhotic accent is said like spider

indicators.note: the river letter goes across the middle of the taxi word, inside it

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a sea animal while their taxi went over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIED A, said 'reportedly' without a sounded R, gives SPIDER; R goes 'crossing' into CAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider crabs are long-legged crabs living on the seabed, so they are sea animals.

clue.text: Bloomer made by teacher going round a new food shop

indicators.note: the teacher word encircles the other pieces

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared food

explanation.surface: A lecturer makes a mistake while touring a new delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or a loaf of bread, both at home in a food shop; here it means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a plant that flowers, and the dandelion is a common yellow-flowered weed.

clue.text: Woman priest, one giving orders?

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A female cleric who may be handing out holy orders.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the pun: a priest might give holy orders, but a director gives instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A director is someone in charge who issues instructions, as of a film or a company.

clue.text: Degrading form of feuding overwhelming one in Scotland

indicators.note: the rearranged letters engulf the Scots word, holding it inside
a new form of the word feuding means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: yin is the Scots word for one

explanation.surface: A demeaning kind of quarrel swamps a solitary Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges FEUDING to UNEDIFG, which is 'overwhelming' YIN, Scots for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Unedifying means morally or culturally unimproving, so a degrading spectacle is an unedifying one.

clue.text: New Zealander's answer you and I heard

indicators.note: signals that the words are said aloud and spelt the way they sound

parts.note: a key is an answer, as to a puzzle, and you and I together are we

explanation.surface: A New Zealander's response, overheard by the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY (answer) plus WE (you and I), 'heard', sounds like the answer. The 's links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiwi is the familiar nickname for a person from New Zealand, after the national bird.

clue.text: Eg Welsh commander-in-chief welcoming English officer

indicators.note: the commander's letters take the others in

parts.note: Lt is lieutenant, a military officer

explanation.surface: A Welsh general receives an English officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh is one of the Celtic languages, along with Irish, Gaelic, Breton and Cornish.

clue.text: Key army corps almost crazy about hotel's liqueur

parts.note: C is a musical key
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the hotel letter
the word for crazy loses its last letter, falling just short

parts.note: demented means crazy
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Military mechanics, half mad, drink a hotel's mint-flavoured spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims DEMENTED to DEMENTE, which goes 'about' H. REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème de menthe is a sweet mint-flavoured spirit drunk after dinner, so it is a liqueur.

clue.text: Racecourse record thus misrepresented at first

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: signals the opening letter of misrepresented

explanation.surface: A track's record is described wrongly to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom, in Surrey, is the English racecourse where the Derby is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a famous horse-racing course in Surrey, England, home of the Derby.

clue.text: Responsibility — and where ours lies

explanation.surface: A reflection on duty and whose shoulders it falls on.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as ON US, where 'ours', our onus, rests.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a duty or burden that rests on someone, so it means responsibility.

clue.text: Work trapeze artistes are ill-advised to have

definitions.meaning: a musical composition for nine players

definitions.text: trapeze artistes are ill-advised to have
definitions.meaning: performing without a safety net is unwise

explanation.surface: A piece of advice for circus performers on what not to take on.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NO NET for the second, cryptic definition; 'Work' is the musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a composition for nine instruments or voices, so it is a musical work.

clue.text: Hint from small Scouse singer inspiring in tango

indicators.note: the singer breathes in the other pieces, taking them inside

parts.note: Cilla Black was a singer from Liverpool, whose natives are called Scousers
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tiny clue from a Liverpool singer who is caught up in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' means breathing in: CILLA takes IN and T. Cilla Black was a Liverpool pop singer and TV host; Scouse means from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or trace amount, so it can mean a hint of something.

clue.text: Drink Scandinavian nomad left unfinished

indicators.note: the nomad word loses its final letter

parts.note: a Lapp is a member of the Sami people of northern Scandinavia, traditionally reindeer herders

explanation.surface: A herdsman of the far north abandons his drink half-finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like an abbreviation for L but belongs with 'unfinished'. Drink is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap is to drink by scooping liquid with the tongue, as a cat does.

clue.text: One who guides bullocks to west of island

indicators.note: in an across clue the first piece sits to the left of the second

parts.note: steers are castrated young bulls, bullocks
the Isle of Man, often just Man

explanation.surface: A drover leads cattle across to the west of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guides' suggests a verb, but 'One who guides' is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A steersman is the person at the helm who steers a boat, guiding its course.

clue.text: Manage to catch son in wood

indicators.note: the word for manage catches the son letter inside it

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in tracking down their boy among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket of trees, a little wood.
